## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. 1	---
     2	id: DOC-EMC-BIOMARKER-SELECTED
     3	title: Biomarker-selected therapeutic classes in an ultra-rare sarcoma — what the available expression data excludes
     4	level: L3
     5	kind: manuscript
     6	status: live
     7	canonical_for: ["the 2026-08-09 EMC biomarker-selected class exclusions"]
     8	purpose: >
     9	  Ask, of five therapeutic classes that are given on a molecular state rather than on a histology,
    10	  whether that state is present in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma — and report that for four of
    11	  them the answer is no, with the strength of each negative stated separately.
    12	scope: >
    13	  L3. Two public archival expression series, 16 EMC tumours, transcript level only, plus a public
    14	  sarcoma-line CRISPR dependency panel containing no EMC line. Reports no experiment in EMC cells, no
    15	  drug exposure and no patient.
    16	audience: [maintainers, external reviewers, autonomous research agents, collaborators]
    17	date: 2026-08-09
    18	last_verified: 2026-08-09
    19	related: [DOC-MODALITY-CENSUS, DOC-EMC-MTAP-PRMT5]
    20	---
    21	
    22	# Biomarker-selected therapeutic classes in an ultra-rare sarcoma
    23	
    24	> ⛔ **Nothing here asserts efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window or clinical readiness for any agent
    25	> in any disease.** This paper reads public transcript data from 16 archival tumours and a public
    26	> dependency panel that contains no cell line from this disease. Every conclusion is a statement about
    27	> whether a *selection criterion* appears to be met, never about whether a drug works.
    28	
    29	---
    30	
    31	## Summary
    32	
    33	Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) is an ultra-rare sarcoma driven by an *NR4A3* gene fusion,
    34	most often **EWSR1::NR4A3**. It has no targeted agent, and its systemic options are few.
    35	
    36	A growing share of oncology's therapeutic classes are given not on a histology but on a **molecular
    37	state** — a lost enzyme, an intact pathway, a repair deficiency. That is structurally good news for an
    38	ultra-rare disease, because it offers entry to a drug developed for someone else. It is only good news
    39	if the state is actually there.
    40	
    41	**We asked that question for five such classes, and for four of them the state is absent.** Each
    42	selecting feature is readable in expression data that has been public for years, and for none of the
    43	five had the lookup been reported.
    44	
    45	⭐ **The useful output of this paper is which classes the data rules OUT.** In a disease with perhaps a
    46	few hundred patients diagnosed per year worldwide, a route that is quietly kept alive on an untested
    47	assumption consumes attention that has nowhere else to come from. **The field publishes almost none of
    48	these exclusions**, so each one gets re-proposed.
    49	
    50	⚠ **The four negatives are not equally strong, and the paper's central methodological claim is that
    51	saying so is the whole job.** One is a clean refutation of the selecting feature. Two are refutations
    52	of a *proxy* for a feature this instrument cannot see. One is a partial reading whose absent half is
    53	precisely the half a transcript cannot measure. They are reported separately for that reason and never
    54	summed.
    55	
    56	---
    57	
    58	## 1 · What was measured, and against what
    59	
    60	**Two public series — the only EMC expression data this array-based reader can score as a group of
    61	tumours.**
    62	
    63	⚠ **That is a statement about the instrument, not about what exists.** The repository's own readability
    64	record names five GEO series carrying EMC-titled samples; three are unread here, and none is read as
    65	absent. GSE28866 (4 EMC) is a 3SEQ deposit whose processed matrix sits in GEO *supplementary* files this
    66	reader never opens and is indexed by peaks rather than genes, so whether a given gene can be read out of
    67	it is UNKNOWN. GSE43632 and GSE80126 hold one EMC sample each, and on neither platform did any probe map
    68	to a gene symbol. One further datapoint sits outside these array series: GSE299349 / GSM9037837, a
    69	patient-derived EMC-*labelled* model whose identity check returned
    70	`LABEL_WEAKLY_CORROBORATED_AND_THE_COMPARISON_IS_CONFOUNDED`. **An absent reading is not a reading of
    71	absence, and sixteen tumours is a defensible choice rather than a ceiling nobody could have exceeded.**
    72	
    73	| series | platform | EMC | comparator arm |
    74	|---|---|---:|---|
    75	| GSE24369 | GPL6244 | 6 | 29 comparator sarcomas, itself including a FET-rearranged histology |
    76	| GSE4303 | GPL3290 | 10 | 6 |
    77	
    78	⚠ **Sample accounting, GSE24369.** The series holds **42** samples: six entered the EMC arm, 29 the
    79	comparator arm, and **seven entered neither.** Two are pooled skeletal-muscle RNA references, correctly
    80	out of a tumour comparator. **Five are solitary fibrous tumours — soft-tissue sarcoma biopsies on the
    81	same array, annotated `sample type: tumor biopsy` like every included comparator — and they are out
    82	because the sample classifier matches substrings and holds no pattern for that histology, not because of
    83	any stated rule about which sarcomas belong in the arm.** Every GPL6244 statistic below is computed
    84	against the reduced arm of 29, and **what the five would do to it is UNKNOWN**: the panel artifact holds
    85	per-sample values for 35 of the 42 and the series matrix is not in this repository, so answering it needs
    86	a re-fetch and a regeneration.
    87	
    88	Genes were read as a *z*-score against each array's own probe distribution; groups scored as the mean
    89	EMC-minus-comparator difference in standard-deviation units, with Welch *t* and no multiplicity
    90	correction. Every figure quoted here is owned by
    91	[`emc-expression-panels.json`](../../modalities/emc-expression-panels.json), and the grading of each class
    92	against its own selection criterion by
    93	[`census-route-expression-grading.json`](../../modalities/census-route-expression-grading.json). Class
    94	definitions are anchored in
    95	[`biomarker-class-definitions-2026-08-09.json`](../../literature/biomarker-class-definitions-2026-08-09.json).
    96	
    97	**A second, independent axis where a class needed one.** Where the question was not "is the feature
    98	present" but "would hitting this target be selective", the sarcoma-line CRISPR dependency panel
    99	([`depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json`](../../modalities/depmap-sarcoma-dependency.json)) was read instead.
   100	⛔ **That panel contains no EMC line** — the one line carrying the disease's label is recorded as not
   101	harbouring the fusion — so every dependency figure here is a **transfer from other sarcomas**, and the
   102	honest bound is not a small sample but no observation in this disease at all.
   103	
   104	⚠ **The proliferation control does not pass on both platforms.** MKI67 was read as an instrument
   105	control, on the expectation that EMC is slow-cycling and that a large proliferation delta would mean the
   106	contrast is being driven by cellularity. It is flat on GPL6244 (+0.13 SD, *t* = 0.53) and **higher in EMC
   107	on GPL3290 by 1.24 SD (*t* = 2.30)**. Three other proliferation-associated transcripts are flat on
   108	GPL3290 (PCNA *t* = 0.13, TOP2A *t* = 0.76, MCM2 *t* = 1.45), so the control fails on one gene on one
   109	platform rather than uniformly — **but it fails, and every GPL3290 reading below must be read with that
   110	open.**
   111	
   112	⚠ **Two standing rules govern every row below.** A gene with no probe mapping is recorded as
   113	*unreadable*, never as unexpressed — an absent reading is not a reading of absence. And a near-universal
   114	dependency is evidence **against** selectivity, not for it.
   115	
   116	## 2 · The five classes
   117	
   118	### 2.1 · Arginine deprivation — the selecting feature reads the wrong way
   119	
   120	Agents in this class are given on **loss of ASS1**, the enzyme that lets a cell make its own arginine;
   121	the argument and its sarcoma-specific evidence are in PMID 27735949 and PMID 28122247, the latter being
   122	the closest published setting to this disease.
   123	
   124	**ASS1 is HIGHER in EMC than in comparator sarcomas on both platforms**, and on GPL6244 it sits at the
   125	92nd percentile of that array's own distribution. The class requires it to be low.
   126	
   127	⚠ **Strength: this is the strongest of the four negatives, and it is still not a proof.** ASS1 loss in
   128	the source literature is an immunohistochemistry call, and a transcript is not a protein. The reading
   129	de-prioritises the class; it does not establish that the class could not act.
   130	
   131	### 2.2 · MDM2 inhibition — the axis reads quiet rather than intact
   132	
   133	This class needs a p53 axis that is both intact **and transcriptionally live**. Reading output rather
   134	than the gene is the point: MDM2 expression is itself *induced by* wild-type p53 activity (PMID
   135	8440237), so the axis's own output is the available proxy for whether it is running.
   136	
   137	**The p53 transcriptional output group is LOWER in EMC on both platforms** (*t* = −2.20 and −1.13),
   138	while the axis genes themselves are flat. Quiet, not live.
   139	
   140	⚠ **Strength: weak, and in a direction worth stating.** A quiet p53 output is not a defective axis — an
   141	unstressed tumour has little p53 output by construction, and these are archival resections. **This
   142	cannot establish that *TP53* is wild-type or mutant, and it does not.** ⭐ It is reported because the
   143	quiet-genome argument that raised this class *predicted the opposite*, and a prediction that fails its
   144	own test should be recorded.
   145	
   146	### 2.3 · EZH2 inhibition — neither selecting shape is present
   147	
   148	The approved agent's registrational indication is selected by **loss of INI1/SMARCB1** (PMID 33035459)
   149	— a SWI/SNF tumour-suppressor subunit — and the neighbouring argument for the class is PRC2 elevation.
   150	
   151	**Neither is there.** EZH2 is mildly higher on both platforms and the rest of PRC2 is flat (*t* = −0.22
   152	and 1.71); **no SWI/SNF tumour-suppressor subunit reads anywhere near a floor** (*t* = −1.02 and −0.08).
   153	
   154	⚠ **Strength: weak, and this is the clearest case of the instrument missing the target.** The approved
   155	indication is selected by protein **loss**, which is frequently post-transcriptional. A normal
   156	transcript does not exclude it. This is reported as a weak negative and should be read as one.
   157	
   158	### 2.4 · Polymerase-θ inhibition — one half present, the other absent
   159	
   160	This class selects on a **combination**: alternative end-joining active while homologous recombination
   161	is deficient. Both halves are established — HR-deficient tumours depend on Polθ-mediated repair (PMID
   162	25642963), Polθ promotes alternative end-joining and suppresses recombination (PMID 25642960) — and the
   163	first-in-class inhibitor selects on the HR-deficient half (PMID 34179826).
   164	
   165	⭐ **The alt-EJ half is present on both platforms.** The alt-EJ module is higher in EMC on both
   166	(*t* = 2.42 and 2.23), every readable member is higher on both, and the non-homologous end-joining
   167	contrast is flat on both (*t* = −0.19 and 0.16) — **so the elevation is specific against NHEJ.**
   168	⚠ **It is not shown to be specific more broadly, and on GPL3290 it is not shown to be specific at all:**
   169	the homologous-recombination module rises *more* than the alt-EJ module there (+0.266 against +0.258 SD),
   170	so the two move together on that platform and only GPL6244 separates them (+0.087 against −0.044).
   171	⚠ **Three of the module's four members are single-strand-break and base-excision-repair factors**
   172	(LIG3, PARP1, XRCC1), and no contrast against that pathway was read. ⚠ **The route's own primary gene is
   173	the weakest reading in the module.** POLQ has no probe on GPL3290, so the module score there is computed
   174	over three of four genes and the drug target contributes nothing; on GPL6244 it is higher by 0.04 SD
   175	(*t* = 0.31) and sits at the **21st percentile** of that array. **The module carries this observation and
   176	the target gene does not.** Nothing in the literature explains the elevation in this disease.
   177	
   178	⛔ **The half that selects the class is not present.** The homologous-recombination arm is flat to mildly
   179	*higher* (*t* = −0.57 and 1.04), not down. The combination is absent, so the class is not indicated.
   180	
   181	⚠ **Strength: the weakest negative in the paper, and its own reason for being weak is decisive.** An HR
   182	**defect** is usually a mutation, and can sit behind entirely normal HR transcript. So the half that came
   183	back negative is precisely the half this instrument is least able to measure. ⭐ **We report the alt-EJ
   184	elevation alongside the negative rather than burying it**, with the limits above attached, because a
   185	reader deciding whether to spend a sequencing run on this disease should have it.
   186	
   187	### 2.5 · BH3-mimetics — the one that survives, and it survives by failing differently
   188	
   189	This class is selected by which anti-apoptotic protein holds the cell's death effectors. That is a
   190	**dependency**, and the method that measures it is BH3 profiling, which reads integrated pathway
   191	function rather than protein level (PMID 17692808, PMID 22230093).
   192	
   193	**On abundance the reading is negative and clean.** All five druggable guardians together are LOWER in
   194	EMC than in comparator sarcomas on both platforms (*t* = −4.57 and −2.54), MCL1 and BCL2L1 individually
   195	included.
   196	
   197	⭐ **But NOXA — the BH3-only protein that specifically neutralises MCL-1 — is higher in EMC by 1.74
   198	standard deviations of that array on GPL3290** (*t* = 7.59; 66 of that array's 14,403 symbols move at
   199	least as hard). ⚠ **On GPL6244 it is directionally higher and flat by this paper's own convention**
   200	(0.23 SD, *t* = 0.63, with 76% of that array's symbols at least as extreme), and there the BH3-only
   201	sensitiser group as a whole is flat-to-lower (*t* = −0.17). **This is a one-platform observation.**
   202	
   203	⛔ **Low guardians with a high sensitiser on GPL3290 would be the transcriptional shadow of a *primed*
   204	cell, and priming is what this class exploits.** So the abundance reading does not refute the class — it
   205	de-prioritises one specific claim about which guardian dominates, while leaving the underlying
   206	hypothesis *more* interesting, not less. **This is the one class of the five that stays open**, and it
   207	stays open because the instrument cannot reach the question rather than because the data was favourable.
   208	
   209	⚠ On the dependency axis, MCL1 and BCL2L1 are dependencies in the large majority of sarcoma lines. That
   210	is a statement about the tissue class, not about EMC, and a near-universal dependency argues against
   211	selectivity rather than for it.
   212	
   213	## 3 · What this paper is not
   214	
   215	- ⛔ **Not a claim that any of these agents would fail in this disease.** Four selection criteria are
   216	  unmet on the evidence available; a class can act through a mechanism its biomarker does not capture.
   217	- ⛔ **Not a substitute for the assays named above.** For all five of them the deciding measurement is
   218	  a protein, a mutation or a functional assay, and each is named in its own section.
   219	- ⛔ **Not generalisable beyond these 16 tumours** on two array platforms of different generations, with
   220	  differing comparator arms, uncorrected for multiple testing.
   221	
   222	## 4 · Falsifiers
   223	
   224	| # | claim | the observation that would kill it |
   225	|---|---|---|
   226	| F1 | ASS1 is not lost in EMC | ASS1 immunohistochemistry showing protein loss in an EMC series, which would override the transcript reading entirely |
   227	| F2 | the p53 axis is not transcriptionally live | a *TP53* sequence call plus a stress-response readout in the same tumours |
   228	| F3 | no SWI/SNF subunit is lost | INI1/SMARCB1 immunohistochemistry in an EMC series — the assay the approved indication actually uses |
   229	| F4 | the HR-down half is absent | a mutational or genomic-scar readout showing homologous-recombination deficiency behind normal transcript — **the single most likely way this paper is wrong** |
   230	| F5 | the alt-EJ elevation is real | a third EMC series in which the alt-EJ module is null or lower |
   231	| F6 | guardian abundance is low with NOXA high | a third series reversing either direction |
   232	| F7 | the apoptotic question is unresolved | BH3 profiling on EMC tissue or a model — **the decisive test, and the one this paper argues is worth running** |
   233	| F8 | none of these readings is a proliferation or cellularity artefact | ⚠ **partly tested and not clean.** The MKI67 control passes on GPL6244 (*t* = 0.53) and fails on GPL3290 (+1.24 SD, *t* = 2.30), with three other proliferation transcripts flat there. A series matched on proliferation, in which the contrasts disappear, would still kill it |
   234	
   235	## 5 · Limits
   236	
   237	- **Sixteen tumours, two decade-old array platforms, uncorrected for multiple testing — and a *t* near 2
   238	  is not remarkable on either array.** The producing artifact scores a Welch *t* for every symbol on each
   239	  platform; against that distribution, transcripts at |*t*| ≈ 2.2 sit where roughly a quarter to a third
   240	  of all symbols sit (0.29–0.32 on GPL6244, 0.26–0.29 on GPL3290), while ASS1 sits at 0.069 and 0.046.
   241	  **That placement controls no error rate and is not a significance claim** — the distribution is
   242	  observed rather than permuted and contains real biology — but it cuts both ways: it makes the four
   243	  negatives harder to overturn and removes any claim of remarkableness from the alt-EJ elevation. Two
   244	  series is not a replication set.
   245	- **A transcript is not a protein, a mutation or a dependency**, and for all five classes the
   246	  selecting feature is one of those three rather than a transcript level.
   247	- **The comparator arm is other sarcoma**, so every statement is relative. A feature could be present in
   248	  EMC and in its comparators alike and would read as absent here.
   249	- **No EMC cell line carrying the fusion appears in any public dependency dataset**, so the dependency
   250	  axis is a transfer from other sarcomas throughout and inherits that limit wherever it is used.
   251	- **Nothing here has been tested in an EMC cell**, and no agent in any of these five classes has been
   252	  given to a patient with this disease.
